name: Berglsteiner See
kurzbeschreibung: The Berglsteiner See at 713 m elevation: hidden woodland lake natural monument between Breitenbach and Kramsach with circular trail, sunbathing lawn, and restaurant.
beschreibung:
Overview

The dreamy Berglsteiner See lies tucked away in dense mixed deciduous woodlands at an elevation of 713 meters on the slopes of the Voldöppberg in the Tyrolean Unterinntal. Situated on the border between the municipalities of Breitenbach am Inn and Kramsach (Kufstein district), this scenic lake spans approximately 2.3 hectares and reaches a maximum depth of around two meters. Owing to its pristine landscape, species-rich shoreline flora, and idyllic tranquility, the woodland lake is designated as a protected Naturdenkmal (natural monument) and is cherished as one of the most enchanting insider tips of the Alpbachtal holiday region.

Natural Monument, Legends & Circular Trail

The Berglsteiner See owes its origin to glacial scouring by the Ice Age Inntalgletscher and sits nestled in a gentle hollow at the base of steep rocky crags. Sheltered by the surrounding forest and relatively shallow, the lake warms rapidly in summer to comfortable temperatures between 22 and 24 °C, creating superb conditions for open-water swimmers. A famous Tyrolean legend enshrouds the waters: two distinctive boulders protruding from the lake are said to be the enchanted lovers Ritter Berglstein and his sweetheart, who drowned due to the arrogance of the castle lord. For walkers and families, a delightful Seerundweg of about one kilometer runs directly alongside reed beds and beneath shady beech canopies (walking time approx. 25 minutes). Rustic benches and wooden viewing platforms along the way provide perfect spots to observe dragonflies, waterfowl, and water lilies. On the eastern shore stands the traditional Restaurant Berglsteiner See 713, featuring a spacious sun terrace perched directly above the water.

Visit & Getting There

The Berglsteiner See and its lakeside circular path are open and freely accessible year-round free of charge. Swimming in the natural lake is permitted free of charge from the designated shoreline sunbathing lawns. The lakeside restaurant operates seasonally from April through late October. By car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Kramsach), travel through Kramsach toward Breitenbach am Inn, following signs for 'Berglsteiner See' up to the hiking parking lot (pay-and-display, day pass approx. €4.00). From the parking area, an easy, roughly ten-minute woodland stroll leads up to the lake. By public transport: train to Brixlegg or Rattenberg-Kramsach station, then bus line 4111 to Kramsach and continue on foot (approx. 45-minute walk from Kramsach-Moosen).

Tips

The short approach from the car park and the circular lakeside path are level and well surfaced, making them wonderful for outings with strollers and active seniors. Stop by Restaurant Berglsteiner See to enjoy homemade Tyrolean dumplings or fresh sheet cake on the lakeside terrace while the rugged crags of the Voldöppberg mirror in the glass-like water.
